cards.subject: The Eastweald
lines: A province of the Kingdom of Lordaeron — farms, roads and small villages. Not Darrowmere, which is the lake and the island west of the river.
It died when Arthas culled Stratholme and the plague ran north out of the city.

cards.subject: There is a necropolis in the sky
lines: Kel'Thuzad's citadel floats above the north of this zone and you can see it from the ground, on this map, in this expansion.
You get in from a runic circle at a spire in Plaguewood, and only if the Argent Dawn has attuned you.
It moves to Northrend in Wrath. In here it is overhead.

cards.subject: The faction is the Argent Dawn
lines: The Argent Crusade does not exist. Tyr's Hand belongs to the Scarlet Crusade and nobody has liberated anything.
Past Tyr's Hand the eastern edge is simply the zone border — New Avalon and the death knight start are Wrath.
The Scourge story here is unfinished, and stays unfinished.

cards.subject: One lit building
lines: Inn, mailbox, stables, anvil, flight master — and neutral, so both factions stand at the same fire in the worst zone in the game.
Every scourgestone you pull off a corpse comes back here.
It is the only fixed point in the Plaguelands.

cards.subject: He is standing in his own dooryard
lines: Marris is his family name and this farm is his. Nathanos was killed here during the Scourging by Ramstein the Gorger.
That is the same abomination you fight as a boss inside Stratholme, up the road.
Sylvanas took him back off the Lich King and sent him home.

cards.subject: Corin's Crossing
lines: A crossroads town packed solid with Scourge and the Cult of the Damned.
Its speciality is invisible, and it sees through stealth.
The wiki's own advice is that rogues should not try to sneak the town.

cards.subject: The spires are not ruins
lines: The crystalline structures over Plaguewood and the glades are not broken Lordaeron buildings. Nothing human ever looked like that.
Nothing else in the Eastern Kingdoms does either.
The only comparable skyline in this zone is the thing floating above it.

cards.subject: The Noxious Glade
cards.tag: Go and stand in the colour
lines: Thick sickly green air sitting over dark purple ground, with ziggurats and a slaughterhouse in it.
It is the most saturated and least natural-looking spot in the zone.
Worth the walk for the palette alone.

cards.subject: Terrordale
cards.tag: Nobody wrote the old name down
lines: A ghost town in the far north-west, reached through a crypt-fiend tunnel.
The wiki says outright it "likely had a much less morbid name before the invasion".
Terrordale is what people started calling it. It is not what it was called.

cards.subject: Quel'Lithien Lodge
lines: A high elven hunting lodge on the road to the sealed gates of Quel'Thalas, held by rangers who refused Silvermoon's new magic and never went home.
In 1.12 they are alive and they will talk to you.
Nearly every one of them becomes Wretched later. You are in the last years of it.

cards.subject: Tyr's Hand
cards.tag: A walled city inside a dead zone
lines: The Scarlet Crusade hold this whole corner — a cathedral, an abbey, walls, a working population, in the middle of the Scourge.
Its Crusaders drop raw coin, so level sixties farmed it for gold for years.
That is what most veterans actually remember it as.

cards.subject: The four towers can be taken
lines: Crown Guard, Eastwall, Northpass and Plaguewood, captured tug-of-war style, and holding them gives your entire faction extra damage against undead in the zone.
It arrived in the final vanilla patch.
Vanilla — but only just.

cards.subject: The gates of Stratholme
lines: The dead city sits on the northern edge and you walk its outside wall to reach it: a main gate, and a service entrance round the side.
Inside, the Scarlet Crusade hold the living quarter and the Baron holds everything else.
From the road it is walls and smoke. It is still burning.
